bench_press.instruction_short_text: Lower bar to chest, then press to full extension
instruction_detail_text: Lie on the bench with eyes roughly under the bar, feet flat on the floor, and a slight arch through the upper back.
Unrack the bar over the shoulders, then lower it under control to the mid-chest while keeping the elbows tucked at roughly 45 degrees from the torso.
Press the bar back up in a straight line to full elbow extension, keeping the shoulder blades pinned to the bench throughout.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the bar and pull it into your palms
Drive your feet into the floor
Keep your shoulder blades pinned together
Bar path straight down to the chest, straight back up
common_faults: Elbows flare out to 90 degrees on the way down — tuck them closer to about 45 degrees from the torso to protect the shoulders.
Hips lift off the bench on heavy reps — keep glutes in contact with the bench throughout the lift.
Bar drifts toward the neck or stomach instead of a straight path — bring it down over the nipple line and press it back up in the same line.

incline_bench_press.instruction_short_text: Lower dumbbells or bar to upper chest, then press to full extension
instruction_detail_text: Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline and lie back with the bar or dumbbells over the upper chest.
Lower the weight under control to the upper chest, keeping the elbows at roughly 45 degrees from the torso.
Press back up to full extension without letting the bar drift forward over the face.
coaching_cues: Bar or dumbbells to the upper chest, not the neck
Keep the incline moderate — steep angles turn this into a shoulder press
Drive through the feet and keep the shoulder blades set
common_faults: Setting the incline too steep turns this into an overhead press and takes tension off the chest — keep it in the 30-45 degree range.
Flaring the elbows to 90 degrees increases shoulder strain — keep them closer to the torso.
Bouncing the weight off the chest instead of controlling the descent — lower for a full 1-2 count.

dumbbell_bench_press.instruction_short_text: Lower dumbbells to chest level, then press to full extension
instruction_detail_text: Lie on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, elbows bent to roughly 45 degrees.
Press both dumbbells up and slightly inward until they nearly touch at the top.
Lower under control back to chest level, keeping the wrists stacked over the elbows throughout.
coaching_cues: Press the dumbbells up and slightly together
Keep the wrists stacked directly over the elbows
Control the dumbbells down — don't let them drop
common_faults: Letting the dumbbells drift out wide at the bottom puts unnecessary strain on the shoulder — keep the forearms roughly vertical.
Losing wrist position under load — keep the wrist stacked over the elbow rather than let it bend back.
Rushing the eccentric and losing control of the dumbbells — lower with the same control used to press.

push_up.instruction_short_text: Lower chest toward floor, then press back to the start position
instruction_detail_text: Set up in a straight plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder width, body in one straight line from head to heels.
Lower the chest toward the floor by bending the elbows, keeping them at roughly 45 degrees from the torso.
Press back up to full extension without letting the hips sag or pike.
coaching_cues: Keep a straight line from head to heels
Brace the core like you're about to be tapped in the stomach
Elbows tracking back at about 45 degrees, not straight out to the sides
common_faults: Hips sag toward the floor as fatigue sets in — brace the core and glutes to keep the body in one line.
Elbows flare straight out to the sides, straining the shoulders — angle them back at roughly 45 degrees.
Only lowering partway — aim for the chest to get close to the floor on every rep for a full range of motion.

machine_chest_press.instruction_short_text: Lower handles under control, then press to full extension
instruction_detail_text: Adjust the seat so the handles sit at mid-chest height and sit back firmly against the pad.
Lower the handles under control to the starting position, keeping the shoulder blades pinned to the pad.
Press the handles forward to full extension without shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
coaching_cues: Set the seat height so the handles line up with mid-chest
Keep the shoulder blades pinned against the pad
Press through a full range of motion, don't lock out and slam
common_faults: Seat height set too high or low changes the pressing angle and shifts stress away from the chest — line the handles up with mid-chest before starting.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears during the press — keep them pulled down and back throughout.
Using momentum to bounce the weight rather than a controlled press-and-return.

single_arm_dumbbell_press.instruction_short_text: Lower dumbbell to chest level, then press to full extension with one arm
instruction_detail_text: Lie on the bench with one dumbbell at chest level, keeping the non-working hand braced on the bench or hip for stability.
Press the dumbbell up to full extension while resisting rotation through the torso.
Lower under control back to chest level and repeat for the set before switching sides.
coaching_cues: Brace the core hard to resist rotating toward the working arm
Press straight up, not across the body
Control the descent — this side is doing all the work alone
common_faults: Letting the torso rotate toward the working side as the weight gets heavy — brace the core and keep the hips square.
Pressing the dumbbell across the midline instead of straight up over the shoulder.
Rushing between reps without resetting the brace, which compounds the rotation fault over a set.

overhead_press.instruction_short_text: Press bar overhead to lockout, then lower under control
instruction_detail_text: Start with the bar at the front of the shoulders, hands just outside shoulder width, elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Press the bar straight up, moving the head back slightly to let the bar pass, then pushing the head through once it clears.
Lock out overhead with the bar over the midfoot, then lower back to the shoulders under control.
coaching_cues: Squeeze your glutes and brace before every rep
Move your head back then through as the bar passes your face
Lock out with the bar stacked over the midfoot, biceps by your ears
common_faults: Leaning back excessively to help the bar clear the face — move the head back and through instead of arching the lower back.
Pressing the bar forward instead of straight up, which ends with it out in front at lockout — the bar path should finish directly over the midfoot.
Flaring the elbows too wide at the start, which limits how well the bar tracks upward.

dumbbell_overhead_press.instruction_short_text: Press dumbbells overhead to lockout, then lower under control
instruction_detail_text: Start with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward or slightly inward.
Press both dumbbells overhead to full extension without arching the lower back excessively.
Lower under control back to shoulder height and repeat.
coaching_cues: Brace the core before pressing
Press the dumbbells up and slightly inward toward each other overhead
Keep the ribcage down rather than flaring it up as you press
common_faults: Arching the lower back to help drive the weight up — brace the core and keep the ribcage stacked over the pelvis.
Pressing the dumbbells out in front instead of straight overhead.
Letting one side lag behind the other on heavier sets — press both sides at the same tempo.

single_arm_overhead_press.instruction_short_text: Press dumbbell overhead to lockout with one arm, then lower under control
instruction_detail_text: Start with one dumbbell at shoulder height, feet set shoulder width for a stable base.
Press the dumbbell straight overhead while resisting the urge to lean or lateral-flex away from the load.
Lower under control back to shoulder height and repeat for the set before switching sides.
coaching_cues: Brace hard through the core to stay upright
Press straight up over the shoulder, not out to the side
Keep the hips level — don't hike the hip on the working side
common_faults: Leaning or side-bending away from the working arm to compensate — brace the core and stay stacked.
Hiking the hip on the working side to help the weight up — keep the pelvis level.
Pressing the dumbbell out and around instead of straight up.

back_squat.instruction_short_text: Squat down to target depth, then stand back up to full extension
instruction_detail_text: Set the bar across the upper back, brace the core, and unrack with feet roughly shoulder width.
Descend by pushing the hips back and bending the knees until reaching target depth, keeping the chest up and the bar over the midfoot.
Drive back up to full extension, keeping the knees tracking in line with the toes throughout.
coaching_cues: Big breath and brace before every rep
Knees track out in line with your toes
Chest up, bar stays over the middle of the foot
common_faults: Knees cave inward on the ascent — actively push them out in line with the toes throughout the lift.
Heels lift off the floor as depth increases — keep weight distributed across the whole foot, not just the toes.
Losing the brace partway through the rep, which lets the chest collapse forward — reset the brace before every rep, not just the first.

goblet_squat.instruction_short_text: Squat down holding the weight at chest height, then stand to full extension
instruction_detail_text: Hold the dumbbell vertically against the chest with both hands cupping the top end.
Squat down between the knees to target depth, keeping the elbows inside the knees at the bottom.
Stand back up to full extension, keeping the weight held tight to the chest throughout.
coaching_cues: Keep the weight glued to your chest
Sit down between your knees, not back onto your heels
Elbows brush the inside of the knees at the bottom
common_faults: Letting the weight drift away from the chest, which pulls the torso forward — keep it pinned tight throughout.
Knees collapsing inward at the bottom — push them out toward the elbows.
Rounding the upper back at depth — keep the chest tall through the full range.

split_squat.instruction_short_text: Lower into the split stance, then drive back up to the start position
instruction_detail_text: Set up in a staggered stance with the rear foot elevated or flat, front foot far enough forward for the shin to stay near vertical at the bottom.
Lower straight down until the rear knee approaches the floor, keeping the torso upright.
Drive through the front foot back up to the start position without the front knee traveling far past the toes.
coaching_cues: Drop straight down, not forward
Keep the torso tall through the whole rep
Drive through the whole front foot, not just the toes
common_faults: Front knee travels well past the toes on descent, shifting the stress forward — set the stance long enough that the shin stays close to vertical.
Torso leans forward excessively — keep the chest tall and the hips under the shoulders.
Pushing off the back foot to help complete the rep — the front leg should be doing the work.

deadlift.instruction_short_text: Pull bar from floor to lockout, then return it under control
instruction_detail_text: Set up with the bar over the midfoot, shins close to the bar, and grip just outside the knees.
Brace the core, flatten the back, and drive the floor away with the legs while keeping the bar close to the shins.
Finish with hips and knees fully extended, then lower the bar back to the floor under control by reversing the same path.
coaching_cues: Bar stays close to the shins the whole way up
Push the floor away rather than pulling the bar up
Hips and shoulders rise together, not hips first
common_faults: Hips shoot up first while the shoulders stay low, turning the pull into a stiff-legged reach — drive the floor away so the hips and shoulders rise together.
Rounding the lower back under load — brace hard and set a flat back before the bar leaves the floor.
Letting the bar drift forward away from the shins, which adds strain and reduces power — keep it dragging up the legs.

kettlebell_deadlift.instruction_short_text: Pull kettlebell from floor to standing lockout, then lower under control
instruction_detail_text: Stand with the kettlebell on the floor between the feet, hips back and shins near vertical.
Grip the handle, brace the core, and drive through the floor to stand to full extension.
Lower the kettlebell back to the floor under control by pushing the hips back first.
coaching_cues: Push the hips back before bending the knees
Keep the kettlebell close to the body throughout
Stand tall at the top — squeeze the glutes
common_faults: Squatting the weight up instead of hinging — push the hips back first so the movement stays a hinge, not a squat.
Letting the kettlebell swing away from the body during the pull — keep it close throughout.
Hyperextending the lower back at the top instead of finishing with a tall, neutral stance.

single_leg_rdl.instruction_short_text: Hinge on one leg until target range, then return to upright balance
instruction_detail_text: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee, holding a light weight or bodyweight only.
Hinge forward at the hip while the free leg extends back, keeping the back flat until reaching the target range.
Return to standing by driving the hips forward, keeping balance on the standing leg throughout.
coaching_cues: Reach the free leg straight back as you hinge forward
Keep the hips square, don't let them rotate open
Keep a soft bend in the standing knee throughout
common_faults: Hips rotate open toward the free leg as balance is lost — keep the hips square to the floor throughout the movement.
Rounding the lower back to reach further — only go as far as a flat back allows.
Locking the standing knee out straight, which makes balance harder — keep a small, consistent bend.

pike_push_up.instruction_short_text: Lower head toward the floor, then press back to the start position
instruction_detail_text: Set up in a pike position with hips lifted high and hands roughly shoulder width, feet closer to the hands than in a standard push-up.
Lower the head toward the floor between the hands by bending the elbows, keeping the hips high throughout.
Press back up to the start position without losing the pike shape.
coaching_cues: Keep the hips lifted high throughout the rep
Lower the crown of the head toward the floor, not the chest
Press through the whole hand, not just the fingers
common_faults: Hips drop toward a standard push-up position as fatigue sets in, taking load off the shoulders — actively keep the hips lifted high.
Only lowering a few inches — aim to bring the head close to the floor for a full range of motion.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides rather than tracking back at an angle.

box_squat.instruction_short_text: Sit back to the box under control, then stand to full extension
instruction_detail_text: Set the box or bench to the target depth and unrack the bar as in a standard back squat.
Descend under control, sitting back onto the box while keeping the shins closer to vertical than in a free squat.
Pause briefly on the box without relaxing the brace, then drive back up to full extension.
coaching_cues: Sit back onto the box, don't drop onto it
Keep the brace on during the pause — don't relax at the bottom
Drive up hard the instant you touch the box
common_faults: Dropping onto the box hard and relaxing the brace — sit back under control and stay tight throughout the pause.
Rocking forward off the box to build momentum before standing — the drive up should come from the legs and hips, not a forward rock.
Setting the box too low for the intended training purpose — box height should match the specific depth being trained.

pin_press.instruction_short_text: Press bar from the pins to lockout, then return it to the pins under control
instruction_detail_text: Set the safety pins at the target height inside the rack and lie on the bench underneath.
Press the bar up from a dead stop on the pins to full extension, keeping the same bar path as a full bench press.
Lower the bar back down to rest fully on the pins under control before the next rep.
coaching_cues: Press hard from a true dead stop — no bounce off the pins
Keep the same elbow angle you'd use in a full bench press
Full extension every rep, don't cut it short
common_faults: Bouncing or jerking the bar off the pins instead of pressing from a true dead stop, which defeats the purpose of the exercise.
Flaring the elbows wide at the bottom because there's no stretch reflex to help — keep the same 45-degree elbow angle used in a full press.
Setting the pins at a height that doesn't match the intended sticking point being trained.

partial_deadlift.instruction_short_text: Pull bar from the set height to lockout, then return under control
instruction_detail_text: Set the bar on blocks or pins at the target starting height, typically at or above knee level.
Set up with a flat back and braced core, then drive through the floor to lockout using the same technique as a full deadlift.
Lower the bar back to the blocks or pins under control before resetting for the next rep.
coaching_cues: Set the same flat back and brace as a full deadlift
Drive the floor away from the very first inch
Keep the bar close to the legs through the whole range
common_faults: Rounding the lower back because the reduced range feels lighter — keep the same brace and flat back discipline as a full deadlift.
Letting the bar drift away from the shins since there's less distance to travel — keep it close throughout.
Using too much weight for the trained range and losing bar control on the way down — lower under control every rep.
